subject: Chemistry
concept_tested: Distinguishing a compound from a homogeneous mixture using fixed composition and separability
stem: A colourless liquid boils at a single fixed temperature at constant pressure. On electrolysis it yields hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed 2 : 1 volume ratio, and the ratio is the same for every sample tested. The liquid is best classified as

options.A: an element
options.B: a homogeneous mixture of hydrogen and oxygen
options.C: a compound
options.D: a heterogeneous mixture

correct_answer_text: a compound

distractor_rationale.A: An element cannot be decomposed into two simpler substances, yet electrolysis yields both hydrogen and oxygen.
distractor_rationale.B: A mixture of the two gases would not be a liquid under ordinary conditions, and the proportions in a mixture could be varied at will, whereas the observed decomposition ratio is the same for every sample.
distractor_rationale.D: A heterogeneous mixture has visibly distinct phases and non uniform composition, neither of which is observed here.

solution: Two pieces of evidence are given and they carry different weight. A single sharp boiling point at constant pressure supports classification as a pure substance under the criteria used in the textbook, since most mixtures boil over a range. It is supporting evidence rather than proof, because certain constant boiling mixtures also boil at a fixed temperature. The decisive evidence is the decomposition ratio, which is fixed at 2 : 1 for every sample tested. A composition that is the same whatever the source is the defining property of a compound. Decomposition into two simpler substances also rules out an element. Taken together the liquid is a compound.
formula_principle: Chemical classification of matter. A compound has a fixed composition by mass, a sharp boiling point at constant pressure, and can be decomposed into simpler substances only by chemical means.
common_misconception: Reading the words hydrogen and oxygen in the stem and concluding mixture, without noticing that the two gases are products of decomposition rather than components physically present. A second error is treating a sharp boiling point on its own as conclusive proof of a compound.

subject: Chemistry
concept_tested: Distinguishing a compound from a homogeneous mixture using fixed composition and separability
stem: A clear single phase liquid is prepared by stirring 5 g of a white solid into 95 g of water. On distillation the sample separates completely into the original solid and water, and its freezing point falls further as more of the solid is added. The sample is best classified as

options.A: a compound
options.B: a homogeneous mixture
options.C: an element
options.D: a heterogeneous mixture

correct_answer_text: a homogeneous mixture

distractor_rationale.A: A compound has a fixed composition and cannot be separated into its constituents by a physical method such as distillation.
distractor_rationale.C: An element is a single kind of substance and cannot be separated into a solid and water.
distractor_rationale.D: The sample is described as clear and single phase, so its composition is uniform throughout.

solution: Complete separation by distillation, which is a physical process, shows the components are not chemically combined. The freezing point changing continuously as more solid is added shows the composition is variable rather than fixed. Being clear and single phase, the sample is uniform. A uniform mixture of variable composition that is separable by physical means is a homogeneous mixture.
formula_principle: Physical separability and variable composition are the two operational tests that identify a mixture.
common_misconception: Treating any clear single phase liquid as a pure substance, and so calling a solution a compound.

subject: Chemistry
concept_tested: Classifying a named substance as element, compound or mixture
stem: Which of the following is a compound?

options.A: Steel
options.B: Ammonia
options.C: Petrol
options.D: Ozone

correct_answer_text: Ammonia

distractor_rationale.A: Steel is an alloy, which is a homogeneous mixture of iron with carbon and other elements in variable proportion.
distractor_rationale.C: Petrol is a mixture of many hydrocarbons and has no fixed composition.
distractor_rationale.D: Ozone is an allotropic form of the element oxygen, so it is an element and not a compound.

solution: Ammonia is NH₃, in which nitrogen and hydrogen are chemically combined in a fixed 1 : 3 atom ratio, so it is a compound. Steel and petrol are mixtures of variable composition. Ozone consists of atoms of a single element only, so despite being triatomic it remains an element.
formula_principle: A compound contains two or more different elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio by mass.
common_misconception: Assuming that any substance whose molecule contains more than one atom must be a compound, which wrongly classifies ozone.

stem: Which set contains only homogeneous mixtures?

options.A: Sea water, muddy water, brass
options.B: Milk, air, brass
options.C: Sugar solution, sand in water, air
options.D: Air, brass, sugar solution

correct_answer_text: Air, brass, sugar solution

distractor_rationale.B: Milk is a colloidal dispersion of fat droplets in water and is classified as heterogeneous in the prescribed textbook.

concept_tested: Identifying a change as physical or chemical from an observation
stem: Which of the following involves a physical change only?

options.A: Rusting of an iron nail in moist air
options.B: Sublimation of solid iodine to iodine vapour
options.C: Burning of magnesium ribbon in air
options.D: Souring of milk

correct_answer_text: Sublimation of solid iodine to iodine vapour

distractor_rationale.A: Rusting forms hydrated iron(III) oxide, a new substance with a new composition, so it is a chemical change.
distractor_rationale.C: Magnesium is converted into magnesium oxide, a different substance, so it is a chemical change.
distractor_rationale.D: Lactose is converted into lactic acid by bacterial action, which is a chemical change.

common_misconception: Treating any change of appearance, such as the violet vapour of iodine, as evidence of a chemical reaction.

concept_tested: Selecting the correct SI base or derived unit for a stated quantity
stem: The SI base unit of amount of substance and the SI derived unit of volume are respectively

options.A: kilogram and cubic metre
options.B: mole and cubic metre
options.C: mole and litre
options.D: gram and litre

correct_answer_text: mole and cubic metre

distractor_rationale.A: The cubic metre is correct, but the kilogram is the SI base unit of mass, not of amount of substance.
distractor_rationale.C: The mole is correct, but the litre is not the SI derived unit of volume.
distractor_rationale.D: The gram is not an SI base unit and the litre is a non SI unit accepted for use with the SI.

common_misconception: Choosing the litre because it is the unit met most often in the laboratory, rather than the SI derived unit.

concept_tested: Applying the volume to amount proportionality from Avogadro's law
stem: Two vessels are held at the same temperature and pressure. The first contains 0.50 mol of oxygen gas and occupies a volume V. The second contains nitrogen gas and occupies a volume 3V. The amount of nitrogen present in the second vessel is

options.A: 0.50 mol
options.B: 1.0 mol
options.C: 3.0 mol
options.D: 1.5 mol

correct_answer_text: 1.5 mol

distractor_rationale.A: Assumes the amount is unchanged by the threefold increase in volume, which contradicts Avogadro's law.
distractor_rationale.B: Obtained by adding 0.50 mol rather than multiplying by three.
distractor_rationale.C: Obtained by using the volume factor as the amount directly, ignoring that the first vessel holds 0.50 mol and not 1 mol.

solution: Since both vessels are at the same temperature and pressure, volume is directly proportional to amount of substance. Trebling the volume trebles the amount, so the nitrogen present is 3 × 0.50 mol = 1.5 mol. The identity of the gas is irrelevant, which is the essential content of Avogadro's law.
formula_principle: Avogadro's law. At constant temperature and pressure the volume of a gas is directly proportional to the amount of substance, so V ∝ n.
common_misconception: Assuming the heavier or lighter gas must be present in a different amount, which imports molar mass into a relation that does not contain it.

subject: Chemistry
concept_tested: Deducing a molecular formula from combining volumes using Avogadro's law
stem: All gaseous volumes below are measured under the same conditions of temperature and pressure. One volume of nitrogen combines with three volumes of hydrogen to give two volumes of ammonia. Taking hydrogen and nitrogen to be diatomic, the molecular formula of ammonia deduced from Avogadro's law is

options.A: NH₂
options.B: N₂H₆
options.C: NH₃
options.D: N₂H₄

correct_answer_text: NH₃

distractor_rationale.A: Two volumes of NH₂ would be formed from one volume of nitrogen, which matches the observed product volume, but they would consume only two volumes of hydrogen rather than the three stated.
distractor_rationale.B: The hydrogen requirement is not the problem here, since N₂H₆ would consume exactly the three volumes of hydrogen stated. The inconsistency is in the product volume: one volume of nitrogen supplies two nitrogen atoms, which would form only one volume of N₂H₆, not the two volumes observed.
distractor_rationale.D: One volume of nitrogen supplies two nitrogen atoms, which would form only one volume of N₂H₄, not the two volumes observed. It would also consume only two volumes of hydrogen rather than three.

solution: By Avogadro's law the volume ratio 1 : 3 : 2 is also the molecule ratio, giving 1 N₂ + 3 H₂ → 2 X. The left side supplies 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms. Distributing these equally between the 2 molecules of X gives 1 nitrogen atom and 3 hydrogen atoms per molecule, so X is NH₃.
formula_principle: Avogadro's law converts a volume ratio directly into a molecule ratio, so the balanced gaseous equation can be read off from the measured volumes.
common_misconception: Reading the coefficient 2 in front of the product as a subscript in the formula, which produces N₂H₆ instead of NH₃.
